question: What did the Vera C. Rubin Observatory show in its first images released in 2025, and what survey is it carrying out?
text:
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s **June 23, 2025 “First Look”** showed the **Trifid and Lagoon nebulae**, two stellar nurseries in the Milky Way, in striking detail. It also revealed a wide view of the **Virgo Cluster region**, with about **10 million galaxies** visible across the full panorama. The same test observations uncovered more than **2,100 previously unknown asteroids**. ([rubinobservatory.org](https://rubinobservatory.org/news/first-imagery-rubin?_bhlid=7cb0dda02ebba89f3b571d956b69c650b2ebed68&utm_source=openai))

Rubin is carrying out the **Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST)**, a 10-year survey that began in late June 2026. It images the southern sky every few nights to build a time-lapse record that will help astronomers track asteroids, catch events such as supernovae, map the Milky Way, and study dark matter and dark energy. ([rubinobservatory.org](https://rubinobservatory.org/for-scientists/rubin-101/the-legacy-survey-of-space-and-time-lsst?utm_source=openai))
